fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The October minutes showed almost all officials saw a growing risk of tightening further. Since then Logan has called for two more hikes and Daly has openly backed raising. A 0.4% rise in October consumer prices moved the argument from whether to hike to how fast, and whether Warsh's Fed takes a 50 bps step.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US hosts this year under its own presidency, and Trump comes to it from a month of leader-level talks held outside the G20. The Kremlin has floated a three-way summit with Putin and Xi, and Trump's trade power slipped ahead of his meeting with Xi.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: This is one of Christine Lagarde's last meetings before she leaves on 7 February, held weeks after Paris and Berlin settled her succession: De Cos as president, Markus Brunnermeier as chief economist. The council sits with France's borrowing premium over Germany at 1.75 points, and the bank on record that markets, not it, should discipline French debt.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee voted unanimously to hike in November, forecasting that inflation will peak at 4.9%, and Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on. October's figures then showed inflation accelerating again, more than two years above target. This meeting settles whether that condition has been met.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, and Washington sold $500 million of euros to join in, as the currency neared the 160 line. The board weighs whether its rate takes over a defence fought so far with reserves, while nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raised profit forecasts on that same weakness.

fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes its latest reading of US GDP, settling how fast the economy grew over the quarter it covers and what any revision does to the earlier estimate.

fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on US personal income and spending, which carries the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It sets the inflation read that rate expectations and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.recent: The release settles how fast prices paid by US households rose over the latest month it covers, and whether consumer spending kept pace with income.
